props.text:
## Your mission

By the end of this tour you will have **launched a rocket**, and along the way met **all eleven slot types** and most of the tricks that make them interesting: shared variables, hidden slots that unlock, flashcards with backs, quizzes that grade themselves, and a progress meter that only moves when *you* do.

A card is a 12-column grid of **slots**. This paragraph is a `text` slot: GitHub-flavored markdown plus KaTeX, inline like $\Delta v = v_e \ln R$ or displayed:

$$\Delta v = v_e \ln\!\left(\frac{m_0}{m_f}\right)$$

That is the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, and it is the engine of this whole notebook.

> **Tip:** `Cmd+Enter` flips between **Edit** and **Study**. Everything below is meant to be *used* in Study mode — and taken apart in Edit mode. Peeking behind the curtain is the point.

props.alt: A small orange-finned rocket climbing across a starfield

props.text:
### Meet `image` — and the grid

On your left: an `image` slot. It takes a `data:` URI (this rocket is an inline SVG, so the notebook stays a single self-contained file), an `https:` URL, or a local file.

Notice the layout: the image is **4 columns** wide and this text is **8**. Any slot can claim a width `w` on the card's 12-column grid, so slots sit side by side and form little dashboards.

This card also has an **accent color** — the stripe you're seeing is set per card, one hex value.

sections.name: The Δv Lab
sections.title: The Δv lab
sections.subtitle: Sliders write, computes derive, prose quotes the numbers, charts move. One card, one scope.

props.text:
### How a reactive card works

Inside a single card, slots share **variables**. Some slots *write* them, some *derive* new ones, some just *read*. NoteBuilder resolves the dependency graph by topological sort — cycles and missing writers are caught at import, so a card can never wedge itself.

The next card is a working launch console:

- two `slider` slots **write** $v_e$ (exhaust velocity) and $R$ (mass ratio),
- two `compute` slots **derive** your $\Delta v$ and your margin against Earth escape,
- a `text` slot **quotes** the live values mid-sentence,
- a `chart` slot **replots** itself on every drag.

And one more thing: the card hides a **secret slot**. It reveals itself only when your $\Delta v$ reaches **11.2 km/s** — Earth escape velocity. Go earn it.

hint.content: Real engines for scale: kerosene/LOX ≈ 3.0 km/s, hydrogen/LOX ≈ 4.4 km/s. `ve` is exhaust velocity.
`R` is the mass ratio: full rocket over empty rocket. R = 15 means 14 parts fuel for every 1 part rocket.

props.text: Right now your rocket manages **{{dv}} km/s**. Earth escape costs **11.2 km/s**, so your margin is **{{margin}} km/s**. This sentence is an ordinary `text` slot — the `{{dv}}` and `{{margin}}` templates re-render on every drag.

props.label: Δv as a function of mass ratio R, at your current engine

props.text:
🌍 → 🌌 **ESCAPE VELOCITY REACHED.** You are leaving Earth.

This slot was here the whole time, carrying a `reveal` verb: *show me only when* `dv >= 11.2`. Reveal conditions read the same card scope as everything else — use them for spoilers, staged hints, or little rewards like this one.

### What you just used

Did you notice $\Delta v$ grows with the **logarithm** of $R$? Piling on fuel helps less and less — the curve bends over. That one insight is why rockets have stages, and you got it by *dragging*, not by reading a paragraph three times.

Variables are strictly **card-scoped**: `ve`, `R`, `dv`, `margin` exist only inside the console card above. Nothing leaks between cards, so every card is a self-contained little machine you can rearrange freely.

Also: both sliders carry a **hint** verb — the small marker next to them hides real-world engine numbers. Hints are for context you want available but not shouting.

sections.name: Flip School
sections.title: Flip school
sections.subtitle: A flashcard is just a card with a back.

props.text:
**Q.** You double your rocket's mass ratio $R$. Why doesn't your $\Delta v$ double?

*Think, then flip the card.*
**A.** Because $\Delta v = v_e \ln R$, and the logarithm is a flattery-proof function: doubling $R$ only *adds* $v_e \ln 2 \approx 0.69\,v_e$.

items: Fuel also has to lift fuel — that's the whole tragedy.
Gains come from better engines ($v_e$) or staging, not just bigger tanks.
A card back can hold **several slots** — this checklist-style list slot is riding along with the answer.

props.text: **Q.** Meta-question about the app itself: a slider *writes* a variable, a compute *derives* one, a chart *reads* them. What stops a card from computing in circles forever?

**A.** The variable graph is resolved by **topological sort**, and a cycle (or a read with no writer) is caught **at import time**: a cycle refuses to load, a read with no writer loads with a warning, rather than either one spinning at runtime.

sections.name: Check Yourself
sections.title: Check yourself
sections.subtitle: Interactive slots remember the reader — never the author.

props.q: Your rocket has $v_e = 3$ km/s and mass ratio $R = e^2 \approx 7.4$. What is your $\Delta v$?
props.explanation: $\Delta v = v_e \ln R = 3 \times \ln(e^2) = 3 \times 2 = 6$ km/s. This `choice` slot grades itself and shows this explanation either way — right or wrong.

props.q: Which slot types can **write** a variable into a card's scope? *(select all that apply — this is a multi-select `choice`)*
options: `slider` — the reader drags a value in
props.explanation: Sliders and computes are the writers. Charts and text templates are pure readers — they react but never feed back.

props.text:
### Flight log — `text-input`

In one or two sentences: what would you *build* with a reactive card? A `text-input` slot collects free-form words and counts toward progress once you've written something.

✅ Logged. Notice this confirmation only appeared **after** you wrote — it carries a `sequential` verb, which keeps a slot hidden until every completable slot above it is done. And your words live in **reader state**: export this notebook and the file stays clean of them.

### Pre-flight checklist — `list`, style `check`

A `list` slot has three styles: bullets (you met one on a flashcard back), numbered (waiting in the last section), and **check** — where every tick is the reader's own progress.

items: Dragged a slider and watched prose + chart react
Flipped both flashcards in Flip School

props.text:
### Burn drill — `problem`

A `problem` slot draws fresh numbers every attempt, checks the typed answer against a formula, and counts toward progress once you have enough right. Press **New numbers** for another one.

props.prompt: A thruster gives **{{a}} m/s²** for **{{t}} s**. How much speed (m/s) does the ship gain?

props.text: The `progress` slot counts every **completable** slot in its scope — here, the whole notebook: quizzes answered, checklists fully ticked, logs written. It can also scope to a single section or chapter. Nothing here moves because the author says so; it moves because *you* did the work.

### All eleven slots — a `table` slot, tabling itself

Every row below is a slot type; every one of them appears live somewhere in this notebook. (Yes, including this table.)

props.text:
### The `code` slot — holding up a mirror

Every card in this notebook is just JSON. Here is (a trimmed version of) **the launch console you played with in Part II** — export this notebook with **⇩** and you'll find the real thing:

items: **The Factory** — seal the Δv console as a card *type*, then stamp fresh copies into any notebook. Stamps are copies, never references.
**Tags & coverage** — this notebook tags every card `learn`/`play`/`drill`/`check`; open the coverage matrix in Study to see the whole map at a glance.
**Share it** — export as a Reader `.html`: one file, opens offline in any browser, your reader's ticks and answers stay on *their* machine.
**Break it on purpose** — in Edit mode, point a compute at a variable nobody writes, and watch the import validator catch you.

props.text: *End of tour. Eleven slots, six verbs, one rocket — and every trick in this file is now yours. `Cmd+Enter` and go build something.* 🚀
